description: Retrieve the readable text content of a text item (OCR DjVuTXT or plain-text file) from the Internet Archive, with length-aware truncation and a continuation pointer for pagination. Suited for public-domain books, documents, scanned periodicals, and transcripts. Use max_chars and char_offset to page through long documents. To confirm the item has a text file first, call ia_get_item with format "DjVuTXT"; its response also gives the mediatype.

char_offset.description: Character offset to start reading from (default 0). To read the next page, add max_chars to the previous char_offset.

identifier.description: Internet Archive item identifier, e.g. "prideprejudice00aust" (Pride and Prejudice). Obtain from ia_search_items results.

max_chars.description: Maximum number of characters to return in this response. Defaults to the server-configured maximum (IA_MAX_SNAPSHOT_CHARS, typically 50 000); a larger value is served at that maximum, with a notice. Lower values reduce token usage.

name: ia_get_text

char_offset.description: Character offset used for this response.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `item_not_found`: The identifier does not exist in the Internet Archive. `no_text_file`: The item exists but contains no readable text file (DjVuTXT or plain-text). `download_forbidden`: Access to this item is restricted — it is in a login-required or limited collection. `archive_unavailable`: The Internet Archive Metadata API or the text file download did not answer within the request timeout, could not be reached, answered HTTP 5xx after retries, 429, or another 4xx, or the metadata response was unreadable. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

has_more.description: True when there is more text beyond this slice. Increment char_offset by max_chars to read the next page.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters this response could hold — the requested max_chars, or the server maximum when the request exceeded it.

notice.description: Set when max_chars exceeded the server maximum (IA_MAX_SNAPSHOT_CHARS) and was served at it, naming the char_offset of the next page, or saying the page reaches the end of the document.

source_file.description: Filename of the source text file fetched from the item.

source_file_bytes.description: Size of the source text file in bytes, from the item manifest — a byte count, not a character count (non-ASCII text takes several bytes per character). Omitted when the manifest lists no size.

text.description: The text slice starting at char_offset up to max_chars characters.

title: Get Internet Archive Item Text
